summary: Corpus diagnostics and hard case caps. Case caps are hard gates in the shape of MF-011's state-space bound: over budget reports and exits nonzero, never trims. No code path drops, filters, samples, or truncates a case to fit a budget. Diagnostics report count per (action, label class), dominant and starved strata, and what varies across the redundant group, classified into unconstrained ordering / interchangeable values / action enabled across equivalent states. Labelers repurposed to diagnostic strata; remediation is a recommendation requiring user approval; named regression traces always retained. Accept path is raising the cap in spec_manifest.yaml with a recorded rationale. Model delta: corpus_gate + AnalyzeCorpus, 8->9 vars, 11->12 actions, deviating from the stale DistillCorpus/corpus_distilled plan fields.

assertions: no code path drops, filters, samples, or truncates a case to fit a budget -- not silently and not with a recorded drop rule. A --distill style opt-in filter is also a failure.
commands: python3 scripts/tla_spec_dev.py --spec-root specs run spec-unit-tests --ticket MF-014

adapters: spec-unit adapter asserting stratification and drop records on a fixture dump

ticket.objective: Corpus diagnostics and HARD CAPS. Cases are never dropped, filtered, sampled, or truncated to fit a budget -- not silently and not with a recorded drop rule. Case caps (max_internal_cases_per_component, max_external_cases_per_action) become hard gates in the same shape as MF-011 state-space bound -- over budget exits nonzero and reports, and caps stay per-program negotiable so raising one with a recorded rationale is the explicit accept path. On failure the diagnostics report the count per (action, label class), which strata dominate, which are starved, and what varies across the redundant group, so the agent can fix the CAUSE. A lopsided corpus is evidence about the representation -- the committed example emits 200 cases for one action and 2 for another, which means the model enumerates redundant interleavings wanting symmetry reduction, a state constraint, or abstraction. The corpus is the symptom; the diagram is the defect. Labelers are retained but repurposed from selection criteria to diagnostic strata. Remediation is a recommendation requiring user approval, never auto-applied. Named regression traces are always retained. SCOPE CHANGE 2026-07-18 by owner direction -- this replaces the former Corpus Distillation scope, which transcribed the modular_fuzzing.md Corpus Discipline section; both were wrong, because filtering to fit a budget under-represents the program and the kill_rate_floor only samples for the damage. references/modular_fuzzing.md is amended in the same change. See tickets/014-corpus-diagnostics-and-caps.md.
ticket.outcome: Shipped as a hard gate, DEVIATING from the desired_actions / model_state fields above (DistillCorpus / corpus_distilled). Those fields were written for the withdrawn Corpus Distillation scope; distillation no longer exists, so there is nothing named DistillCorpus to model and no corpus_distilled fact to record. Staleness class tracked as deviation here rather than inventing a model change is MF-017. What landed: scripts/corpus_diagnostics.py, wired as a post-write gate in generate_cases_from_tlc_dump.py, a pre-selection gate in export_testgraph_cases.py, and the `tla-spec-dev analyze corpus` command. Model delta is NOT zero: corpus_gate (a 3-valued global verdict) plus the AnalyzeCorpus action, 8 -> 9 variables, 11 -> 12 actions, bound 221,184 -> 663,552, distinct states 2,923 -> 9,011, depth 23 -> 24, all within budget. The growth is deliberate -- an unrepresented gate is not a gate, and hiding a real command to hold a count down is the under-representation this ticket's own doctrine forbids. NOTHING IS DROPPED: no code path removes a case to satisfy a cap. Generation writes the complete package BEFORE the gate runs, and the export gate measures the full corpus BEFORE --label/--case/--limit selection, so no flag can bring a corpus under cap. corpus_gate deliberately has no override; the accept path is raising the cap in spec_manifest.yaml with a recorded rationale, which the failure output prints as a ready-to-paste block. Two findings reported rather than worked around. (1) The 732-case corpus the ticket names as a committed fixture is NOT committed -- that path holds 4 traces; 732 is a run-time figure documented in four reference files. tests/corpus_fixtures.py reconstructs the documented distribution and is labelled a fixture. (2) scripts/extract_spec_manifest.py could not parse a wrapped plain-scalar list item, and since PyYAML is absent in this environment that fallback parser is the only one -- every budget gate was silently degrading to documented defaults, which would have made this ticket's cap-raise accept path a no-op. Fixed minimally; the fallback-with-warning policy itself is untouched and stays with MF-023. Spec-case execution deferred epic-wide; see deferred-validations.md. The C1 action-count finding goes 11 -> 12 and was NOT worked around with --allow-over-budget or by renegotiating component budgets. - max_internal_cases_per_component and max_external_cases_per_action are hard gates read through scripts/budgets.py -- over budget exits nonzero and reports. - raising a cap with a recorded one-line rationale is supported as the explicit accept path. - on cap failure the diagnostics report count per (action, label class), dominant strata, starved strata, and what varies across the redundant group. - labelers are retained as diagnostic strata; no labeler output selects which cases survive. - remediation output is a recommendation requiring user approval, never auto-applied. - named regression traces are always retained. - references/modular_fuzzing.md Corpus Discipline matches what shipped. evidence: []
